items.q: And I stayed with Machito -- went to Japan with Machito. I stayed with him, recorded with him quite a long time after that.

ctx.x: And I stayed with Machito -- went to Japan with Machito. I stayed with him, recorded with him quite a long time after that. And I liked it but I still wanted to play jazz but there wasn't any work.
Oh, so you went into Latin music because of lack of work --

items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: That was Doc Cheatham and Mario and the saxophone was Johnny Nieto

ctx.x: Okay. When you and Mario got together, who were your trumpet players then?
That was Doc Cheatham and Mario and the saxophone was Johnny Nieto, Freddy Skerrittand Pin Madera.
Okay, later on came Bobby Woodlen, right?

items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: He was in the audience when I played in LaBamba, in Machito’s band, a big band.

ctx.x: He was in the audience when I played in LaBamba, in Machito’s band, a big band. We invited, Machito invited Erroll Garner to play. And I say Erroll Garner misunderstood, he didn’t mean for him to play, but introduced him to the audience. And Erroll Garner got up and came up to the piano, you know. I dare say. And after he got up there they put all that Latin music in front of him like “Renee Root.” He set down and played everything, every one of those parts.
